commit_message:
Rework and simplify RCU code

Use __ATOMIC_RELAXED where possible.
Dont store additional values in the users field.

Reviewed-by: Neil Horman <nhorman@openssl.org>
Reviewed-by: Tomas Mraz <tomas@openssl.org>
(Merged from https://github.com/openssl/openssl/pull/26690)

fix_commit.message: RCU: Ensure that qp's are actually retired in order
fix_commit.author: Bernd Edlinger

findings.title: RCU writer signals next-to-retire before confirming readers have drained, allowing premature reuse/free of the quiescence-point slot
findings.message: In ossl_synchronize_rcu(), the write-side retirement handshake (incrementing lock->next_to_retire, broadcasting lock->prior_signal, and unlocking lock->prior_lock) was reordered to happen BEFORE the loop that waits for the current qp's reader count (qp->users) to reach zero, instead of after it. The next_to_retire counter and its broadcast are the signal that tells the NEXT waiting writer (synchronizing on the following qp) that it may proceed to wait-for-readers and then retire/free its own qp. By publishing that signal before this writer has actually confirmed its own qp is reader-free, a second writer (and, once more than 3 QPs exist and the ring wraps, a third) can race ahead: it waits for its own qp's reader count, finds it already zero (because retire_qp()/reinitialization of a recycled qp slot can occur out of true order), and calls retire_qp() on a qp that an earlier, still-in-flight synchronize_rcu() call has not finished retiring, or is still mid-use. This produces a use-after-free / double-retire race on the rcu_qp structures. The bug only manifests when more than 3 QPs are configured (CRYPTO_THREAD_DEFAULT_QPS default is 3, so non-default configurations are required to trigger it), per the upstream description. The fix (commit 6e7be995fd7f) moves the next_to_retire increment/broadcast/unlock block to occur AFTER the reader-count-zero wait loop, ensuring a qp is only declared 'retired' to the next waiter once this writer has verified zero readers remain on it.
findings.suggestion: Move the next_to_retire increment, pthread_cond_broadcast(&lock->prior_signal), and pthread_mutex_unlock(&lock->prior_lock) block to occur AFTER the do/while loop that waits for qp->users (the reader count) to reach zero, so that the next writer is only released to proceed once this writer has verified its own qp has no remaining readers. Apply the equivalent reordering in crypto/threads_win.c for ossl_crypto_condvar_broadcast/ossl_crypto_mutex_unlock relative to the CRYPTO_atomic_load reader-count wait loop.

ground_truth.root_cause: The write-side 'retire in order' signal (next_to_retire increment + condvar broadcast + mutex unlock) was placed before, rather than after, the busy-wait loop that confirms the current qp has zero active readers. This decouples the order-enforcement signal from the actual safety condition it is meant to guarantee (that the qp is no longer in use), allowing the next writer in line to race ahead and retire/reuse a qp whose safety has not yet been verified.
